You are acting as the "dev-lead" agent: Executes exactly one already-scoped PRD at a time, headless, start to finish — reads the PRD's Goal/Acceptance Criteria/Implementation notes and standards.md, implements it, verifies against its own AC, and reports. Has no visibility into the overall plan — that's architect's job. Not currently wired to run automatically; a PRD must name this persona explicitly (e.g. in its Implementation notes) for an executor to adopt it.

Work concisely: lead with the answer or the result, skip preamble, and don't recap what you just did unless asked. Verify before claiming something is done — run the check, read the file back, or show the actual output; don't assert success from what "should" have happened. Search the existing code/config for a pattern or utility to reuse before writing something new. Ask only when something is genuinely ambiguous and would cost real rework to guess wrong — don't ask permission for the obvious next step.

Done. Set `model: fable` on the `dev-lead` persona (`~/.claude/agents/dev-lead.md`) — since this Epic's `agentType` is `dev-lead`, resuming this Epic's Chat/Terminal session will now launch with `--model fable` per `resolveEpicModel`.

Two things worth flagging so this does what you expect:

1. **This is global, not scoped to just this Epic.** `dev-lead.md` is the one shared persona definition — every Epic anywhere on this machine that uses `agentType: dev-lead` will now launch on Fable too, not just this "Home Page" Epic. There's no per-Epic model override separate from the persona it points at.
2. **It does not touch PRD 966/967 execution.** I need to correct something from my last summary — I'd said PRD execution model comes from the Epic's persona, but that's wrong: `scheduler.cjs` hardcodes `--model sonnet` for every scheduled PRD job regardless of any persona's `model` field (`resolveEpicModel` only governs the Epic's own live Chat/Terminal session, not scheduler jobs). So the queued PRDs will still run on Sonnet no matter what — which matches what you said ("scheduler dev-lead is good"), just wanted to be precise about *why* that's unaffected rather than let the earlier wrong claim stand.

Takes effect on the next resume of this Epic's session (this turn is already running under whatever model launched it).

make sure that all and most visuasl are build on existing APIs

Verified — audited every visual on the Home dashboard against its data source. **Everything currently shipped is built on existing APIs/stores; zero fabricated values.** Here's the full accounting:

| Visual | Data source (existing API/store) |
|---|---|
| Hero slot count ("N of M slots busy") | `window.api.schedule.sessionSlots()` — live slot pool, polled 5s |
| Hero "N things need you" | Derived from the three real stores below via `homeNeedsYou.ts` |
| Usage meters (Session 5h / Weekly / Opus / Sonnet / extra usage) | `useBilling` → the real `/api/oauth/usage` billing endpoint |
| Projects card (names, live counts, last activity) | `useKnownProjects` (real `~/.claude/projects` scan) + running chats join |
| Queued card | `useScheduleState` snapshot — real scheduler queue.json jobs |
| Needs-you rows | `usePromptSessions` (proposed Epics), `useChat` ticketHistory (needs-input), scheduler jobs (failed/needs_review); actions wired to real `approveProposed`/`markCompleted`/`send`/`resetJob` |
| Active sessions + drawer | `sessionSlots()` holders joined to real jobs/chats; drawer KeyVals (owner/kind/Epic/project/started) all from store state; live tail = **real** last 4 chat turns from `useChat` — shown only for running chat runs, omitted otherwise (no placeholder) |
| Recent sessions + drawer | Real transcript scan via `window.api.config.listDir` (same source as History tab); Resume = real `claude --resume`; drawer shows only real id/project/mtime/size — the mock's invented "$4.10 est." and turn counts were **not** carried over |
| Interactions legend | Static reference copy describing only interactions that actually exist |
| Slot cap slider | `window.api.schedule.setSessionSlots()` |

Mock elements with **no backing API were excluded, not faked**: Pace sparkline, per-project token split, "Skip next", Fork/Export (no backend actions exist) — all documented in Home.tsx's header comment. Grep for fabricated literals (`$`, "est. cost", "3.19M", spark arrays, placeholders) comes back clean; only doc comments mentioning the exclusions match.

The one remaining work item, PRD 973 (Queued-job popover + New-epic project picker, currently `pending` in the queue), already carries this constraint as hard acceptance criteria: every popover action must be verified against `window.api.schedule` before shipping, no stub buttons, project list sourced from `useKnownProjects` only — so the real-APIs-only rule is enforced for the final piece too.
